messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Private connectivity alert for VPC peering (peer-1234) between rw-infra-eu and customer-corp. Multiple route withdrawals observed originating from eu-west1a (az3). Customer API (api.customer-corp.com) showing ~40% 5xx. Severity: P1. Please acknowledge and join this thread for triage. Link: https://internal.incidents/2901234567

sre_oncall: Ack, I'm on it. Adding netops and eng-runtime. Starting initial triage: gathering peering logs and BGP state.

alex.s: I pulled the peering logs — seeing frequent BGP NOTIFYs and intermittent route withdrawals. Last withdrawal at 2026-03-15T11:22:34Z (root msg ts). Traceroute to peer IP 10.200.10.1 shows spikes then packet loss around hop 5.

netops: Provider console shows the peering control-plane flapping: ESTABLISHED -> DEGRADED -> DOWN -> ESTABLISHED repeatedly. No obvious config churn on our side. Opening vendor ticket now (case# 987654). Also checking for maintenance events in eu-west1a.

maria_p: I messaged the customer SRE (cust-sre) — asking them to hold any config pushes and to check their edge router resource usage. Also recommending they prepare alternate region failover.

cust-sre: Confirmed, we see the withdraws and high errors. Our LB is sticky; existing TCP sessions are dropping. We've started redirecting a small % of traffic to our backup peering in us-west2 but traffic preferences still point to eu-west1a. We'll pause config pushes and send logs.

sre_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Preference shift: bias our edge to prefer backup peering (peer-5678) for customer prefixes to remove degenerated path.
2) DNS TTL: lower TTL for api.customer-corp.com to 30s to speed cutover.
3) Customer: ask for session drain on LB and hold on BGP resets.
4) If provider recommends, migrate peering to a different host.
Executing step 1 now.

sre_oncall: Running command to set route preference (apologies for noisy logs):
```bash
# prefer backup peer for customer prefix
routectl set-preference --peer peer-5678 --prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --metric 200
```

deploy-bot: Route preference updated: peer-5678 now preferred for 203.0.113.0/24 (applied by sre_oncall). :white_check_mark: 

alex.s: Start synthetic checks against api.customer-corp.com -> request latency spikes reduced and error rate dropped to ~10% after the route preference change. Still seeing some 502s due to in-flight TCP sessions on customer side.

netops: Vendor updated ticket: found ECC on host NIC causing sporadic control-plane resets. They propose moving the peering to a different physical host in the same AZ; estimated migration in 10-15 minutes. If migration fails, next step is planned migration to a different AZ.

cust-sre: We've changed DNS TTL to 30s and initiated LB session drain. Starting traffic failover: shifting 30% to us-west2 canary. Monitoring.

sre_oncall: Notes on follow-up commands and checks (for audit):
```bash
# BGP table snapshot after pref change
bgpctl show routes peer-5678 | grep 203.0.113.0/24
# verify peer state
ssh jump-edge "vtysh -c 'show ip bgp neighbors 10.200.10.1'"
```
Logs: saw route re-advertisement at +120s and steady state after +240s.

alex.s: Canary metrics: error rate for canary -> 2%, overall cluster -> 6%. Customer reports external clients seeing improved connectivity for new sessions. Old sessions still fail until clients reconnect (expected).

netops: Vendor confirms migration completed at 2026-03-15T11:35:10Z. Control-plane stabilized; no further NOTIFYs. They will keep the peer on new host and monitor for 1 hour.

maria_p: Good. I'll own post-incident follow-up with the customer and vendor. Capturing timeline and asking customer to run connection tests for long-lived sessions.

sre_oncall: Rolling update to incident status: partial mitigation successful. Customer-facing error rate dropped from ~40% -> ~5-10%. Reasonable to mark as degraded but stable. Keeping P1 until all long-lived session issues are resolved and backup path is confirmed.

cust-sre: We're continuing TCP session drain; long-lived sessions are reducing. No new client complaints in last 12 minutes. Thank you for the quick response.

oncall-next: I'll take watch for the next 60 minutes and perform periodic checks. Please add any open actions you want me to own at handoff.

sre_oncall: Handoff summary for oncall-next:@oncall-next - please monitor: 1) vendor ticket #987654 for any regressions, 2) BGP state for peer-1234 and peer-5678, 3) error rates for api.customer-corp.com (SLO panel link). Action items: maria_p to run postmortem, cust-sre to validate client reconnect behavior. Handoff time: 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident state updated -> MONITORING. Resolved action: route preference override applied, provider migrated peering host, DNS TTL lowered, customer performed LB drain. Owner for follow-up: maria_p. Closing notes will be in postmortem.

maria_p: I'll schedule postmortem and include vendor timeline and recommended guardrails: automated route-preference on control-plane anomalies, and a TTL-drop runbook for customers in similar scenarios.

sre_oncall: Marking initial thread closed from active paging. If regressions occur, reopen and alert oncall. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
